tse.title: Cash, POS and TSE

was-ist-eine-tse.q: What is a TSE and when do I need one?
a: A TSE (technische Sicherheitseinrichtung, a technical security system) is a certified component that protects the records of an electronic cash register against later changes. It is required by German law: § 146a of the Fiscal Code (Abgabenordnung, AO) and the Cash Register Security Ordinance (KassenSichV).

You need a TSE if you take payments with an electronic system that can accept cash – the law calls this a “cash register function” (Kassenfunktion). According to the German Federal Ministry of Finance, it is enough that you can switch cash payment on yourself; whether you actually do so makes no difference. Vouchers, prepaid cards or tokens accepted on site count as cash.
A pure ordering system without a cash register module has no cash register function. How that works with OpenEOS is explained under <order>“Orders only”</order>.

This also applies to clubs and club festivals; legal form and non-profit status make no difference. Selling food and drinks at a festival is usually a taxable business activity (wirtschaftlicher Geschäftsbetrieb). If you use an electronic register with a cash register function for it, it needs a TSE – even if it only runs a few times a year. There is no exemption for occasional use.
Violations are administrative offences and can be fined up to € 25,000.

bargeldlos.q: Can I use OpenEOS without a TSE?
a: Yes. In Germany you choose one of two operating modes in which there is no cash in OpenEOS:
“Orders only” (Nur Bons): take orders, kitchen, pickup and order tickets – without prices and without payments. Payment happens outside OpenEOS, e.g. with an open cash box or tokens.
“Cashless” (Bargeldlos): all features with card payments (SumUp) and online prepayment. There is no cash in OpenEOS.

According to the German Federal Ministry of Finance, a cash register function already exists if your club can switch cash on itself. That is why the third operating mode, “All features” with cash, can only be chosen in Germany with an active cloud TSE. You can switch between “Orders only” and “Cashless” yourself at any time under Settings → Organization → Operating mode – that does not bring cash back.

For your system documentation (Verfahrensdokumentation) you can download a manufacturer certificate (PDF) in both modes. It confirms that cash cannot be recorded in your organization and is only possible with an active certified TSE. In individual cases your tax office decides.
If you want to accept cash with OpenEOS, choose “All features” with the <integration>cloud TSE</integration>. More about all three operating modes in the <modesdocs>documentation</modesdocs>.

a.4: If you want to accept cash with OpenEOS, you need a TSE. The <integration>cloud TSE</integration> is coming soon. More about all three operating modes in the <modesdocs>documentation</modesdocs>.

nur-bestellen.q: Can I use OpenEOS for ordering only?
a: Yes, with the “Orders only” operating mode (Nur Bons): take orders, kitchen, pickup and order tickets – without prices and without payments. Payment happens outside OpenEOS, e.g. with an open cash box or tokens.

OpenEOS takes the orders and passes them on to your stations, for example the kitchen and the bar. At the counter you complete an order with “Picked up”, in table service with “Close table”. The till, tickets and customer display show no prices, reports show quantities only. Orders in the online shop or via QR code, deposits and discounts are not available in this mode; the shop shows “orders on site only”.
The money you take on site is subject to the record-keeping obligations of an <ladenkasse>open cash box</ladenkasse>.

As an admin you choose the operating mode yourself under Settings → Organization → Operating mode and can switch it at any time. According to the German Federal Ministry of Finance, ordering systems without a cash register module are not subject to the TSE requirement. In Germany you get a manufacturer certificate for your system documentation.
What exactly the mode covers is described in the <modesdocs>documentation</modesdocs>. Or <contact>write to us</contact>.

bargeld.q: Can I still accept cash with OpenEOS?
a: Yes, with the “All features” operating mode (Alle Funktionen): cash, card and online payment. Whether you can choose it depends on your organization’s country.

In Germany a register that can accept cash needs a TSE. “All features” is therefore only available there with an active cloud TSE; it is included in the price of your event and set up automatically. Without a TSE you choose “Orders only” or “Cashless” and take cash outside OpenEOS, for example in an open cash box.

Organizations that existed before keep working as before as “All features (existing)” – also in Germany, until you pick an operating mode. A notice in the dashboard and in the settings explains the TSE requirement and asks you to choose the country and operating mode. Whether you record cash in OpenEOS without a TSE until then is your own decision; ideally check with your tax advisor. Once you pick another mode in Germany, you can only go back to “All features” with an active TSE.
In Austria, Switzerland and other countries you can choose “All features” without a TSE as well. What applies there is described under Does this also apply in Austria and Switzerland?

a.1: In Germany a register that can accept cash needs a TSE. “All features” is therefore only available there with an active cloud TSE – and that is coming soon. Until then you choose “Orders only” or “Cashless” and take cash outside OpenEOS, for example in an open cash box.

laender.q: Does this also apply in Austria and Switzerland?
a: No, the TSE requirement is a German rule – other countries have their own regulations. That is why every organization in OpenEOS has a country. It is required: new organizations choose it when registering or when they are created, existing ones are asked once. After that only our support can change it.
Outside Germany you can choose all three operating modes freely – “All features” with cash also without a TSE.

Austria: The cash register obligation (RKSV) applies from €15,000 annual turnover per business if more than €7,500 of it is cash turnover. Card payments count as cash turnover in Austria – also in the “Cashless” mode. OpenEOS currently creates no RKSV signature. Exemptions exist, for example, for small festivals of non-profit clubs of up to 72 hours per calendar year and for canteens of non-profit clubs up to €45,000 annual turnover (net, on at most 52 days a year; limit since 2026). More on the Austrian business service portal (USP).
Switzerland: To our knowledge there is no general cash register or fiscalisation obligation. Record-keeping and VAT rules still apply to clubs.
Other countries: Many countries have their own rules for tills (e.g. Italy, France, Poland, Czechia). Check yourself whether OpenEOS is permissible for you there.

In any case, check yourself or with your tax advisor whether OpenEOS is permissible for your club and which obligations apply. This is not tax advice. More in the <modesdocs>documentation</modesdocs>.

offene-ladenkasse.q: What about an open cash box (offene Ladenkasse)?
a: An open cash box – cash in a box, without an electronic register – is allowed. You then need no TSE and don’t have to issue receipts. The record-keeping obligations under § 146 AO still apply. In practice this means:
Record daily: you record the cash box’s takings and expenses on every day you sell (§ 146 (1) sentence 2 AO).

No itemised records needed: if you sell goods such as food and drinks for cash to many guests you don’t know, you don’t have to note every single sale (§ 146 (1) sentence 3 AO). This only applies as long as you don’t use an electronic register for it.

Cash report (Kassenbericht): at the end of the day you count the cash and work out the takings backwards: counted closing balance − opening balance (float) + expenses paid from the box + withdrawals − deposits = daily takings. A counting record listing the notes and coins helps you prove it.
Receipts: every expense, deposit and withdrawal needs a voucher, for example the float taken from the bank account, the purchase from the drinks supplier or the hand-over to the treasurer.
Retention: keep cash reports, counting records and vouchers as required by § 147 AO, 8 to 10 years depending on the document.
If a festival has several cash points, such as bar, grill and token sales, it’s best to count them separately and combine them in the cash report.

tse-integration.q: How do I get the cloud TSE?
a: OpenEOS connects a certified cloud TSE – you don’t need any extra hardware. If you choose the “All features” operating mode in Germany and activate an event, OpenEOS sets up the TSE automatically. All your devices then work as one shared register.

The cloud TSE is included in the price of your event day. All you need is your organization’s tax number or VAT ID and its address. More about the operating modes in the <modesdocs>documentation</modesdocs>.

soon.q: When is the cloud TSE coming?

a.0: The cloud TSE for cash payments in Germany is coming soon. It will let you choose the “All features” operating mode in Germany and accept cash with OpenEOS – without extra hardware, included in the price of your event day.
a.1: Until then you can use <notse>“Orders only” or “Cashless”</notse>. As soon as the cloud TSE is available, we’ll announce it under <changelog>What’s new</changelog>.

tse.note: General information, not tax or legal advice. As of 9 November 2026. Whether and how the rules apply to your club is best clarified with your tax advisor.

a: OpenEOS is a POS system for clubs, events and festival catering. From the club fête to the large-scale event, it covers planning, ordering, kitchen, checkout and reporting in one system – flexible, mobile and open source.
The main building blocks:
Mobile POS on phone or tablet, anywhere on the venue
Self-ordering: guests order via QR code themselves
Kitchen display with a real-time view for kitchen and pickup
Customer display where your guests see their order live
Card payments via SumUp
Automatic receipt printing via the OpenEOS printer agent on a Windows or Linux PC
Floor plan you draw in the admin area and the POS picks up
Shift planning: volunteers sign up via a link, no account needed
Real-time analytics and reports
See what it looks like in <screens>A look inside</screens>.
Registering your organization takes just a few minutes, and there is no setup fee. Your first event is possible right away. Would you rather see it in action first? Then <demo>request a demo</demo>.
There are two ways:
Self-hosted: free, forever. You run OpenEOS on your own server – with all features, one organization, unlimited events and community support.
SaaS: € 25 per event day. All features, hosting, backups, automatic updates, support and the cloud TSE for cash in Germany are included.
No setup fee, no minimum term, no hidden costs. You get a 20% starter bonus on your first event. All details are under <pricing>Pricing</pricing>.

1: Self-hosted: free, forever. You run OpenEOS on your own server – with all features, one organization, unlimited events and community support.
SaaS: € 25 per event day. All features, hosting, backups, automatic updates and support are included – as is the cloud TSE for cash in Germany, once it is available.

event-tag.q: What counts as an event day, and when do I pay?
a: An event day runs from 6:00 to 6:00 – the night counts towards the day before. You pay by card or direct debit when you activate an event. Cancellation is free up to 7 days before the start.
Yes, 100%. OpenEOS is released under the AGPLv3 license: you can self-host it, customize it and contribute. The source code is on <github>GitHub</github>.

Yes. The self-hosted edition is free and includes all features – for one organization with unlimited events. It runs on your own server, and you keep full control over your data. Help comes from the community; the guide is in the <selfhost>documentation</selfhost>.

In the hosted service, the platform and database run on a server of IONOS SE. Once a day, an encrypted backup (AES-256) is sent to a data centre of Hetzner Online GmbH in Germany. Daily backups are kept for 14 days and weekly ones for eight weeks, then they are deleted automatically.
If you run OpenEOS yourself, the data stays on your own server. All details are in the <privacy>privacy policy</privacy>.

gaeste-und-helfer.q: Who is responsible for the data of my guests and volunteers?
a: Your organization. We process your guests’ orders and your volunteers’ data on your behalf (Art. 28 GDPR).

Card payments go through your own SumUp account. OpenEOS only sends SumUp the amount, currency, a description and a transaction number. Your guests enter their card details directly on the card terminal or on SumUp’s payment page.

The POS runs on phones and tablets. OpenEOS prints receipts via the OpenEOS printer agent: it runs on a Windows or Linux PC (Raspberry Pi included), finds your USB and network printers automatically – everything is set up in the web app. For kitchen and pickup you use a display, and optionally a customer display for your guests.
You bring your own devices: ESC/POS receipt printers with a USB or network connection, tablets or phones for the POS, and any device with a browser for the displays.

internet.q: Do I need an internet connection on site?
a: The POS, kitchen display and printers work together through the OpenEOS server. That’s why every device needs a connection to it – with the hosted service, that means internet.
If there is no internet on site, a mobile hotspot or an LTE router of your club is enough – all devices simply join that network.

dataAct.metaTitle: Data Act: locations, data export and switching — OpenEOS
dataAct.metaDescription: Where OpenEOS processes your data, how we protect it against access from third countries, which export formats you get and how switching to another provider works.
dataAct.sub: Information under the EU Data Act (Regulation (EU) 2023/2854) about OpenEOS as a cloud service: locations, protection against third-country access, export formats and switching providers.
dataAct.note: This page summarizes the information in plain language. The binding documents are the <agb>terms (AGB)</agb> (clause 10) and the <avv>data processing agreement</avv> (annex 2 with the list of subprocessors), both in German.

provider.title: Provider and jurisdiction
provider.p1: OpenEOS is a product of LUXCODE by Lukas Lukic-Spitznagel, based in St. Georgen im Schwarzwald, Germany. Your contract is with LUXCODE and governed by German law (terms, clause 14.2).
provider.p2: LUXCODE's support work takes place at its registered office in Germany. No customer data is stored there permanently – it stays in the data centers listed below.

locations.title: Where your data is processed
locations.intro: Your data is stored in data centers in Germany. We use these service providers:

ai: Assistant features (menu import, icon suggestions) – only if you turn them on
tse: Cloud TSE – only if you use it
Swissbit AG, Bronschhofen (Switzerland; EU adequacy decision)
cdn: DNS and upstream service (routing, caching, protection against overload attacks)

locations.outro: Cloudflare and Sentry are based in the USA and are therefore also subject to US law. The European Commission's standard contractual clauses and the EU-US Data Privacy Framework apply to both. All other processing takes place in the EU or EEA. The current list is in the <avv>data processing agreement, annex B</avv>.

protection.title: Protection against third-country access
protection.intro: To keep authorities outside the EU from unlawfully accessing your data, we rely on:
items: Storage in Germany with German companies (IONOS, Hetzner). Error diagnostics with Sentry run in the EU data region.
Encryption in transit: every connection between devices, software, TSE and interfaces uses TLS 1.2 or higher; unencrypted connections are rejected.

Encryption at rest: encrypted storage; backups are encrypted with AES-256 before they are transferred to Hetzner. Credentials (e.g. for the Cloud TSE and your payment providers) and two-factor secrets are stored encrypted; passwords, POS PINs and API tokens only as hashes.
The keys stay with LUXCODE – no service provider gets them.

Review of disclosure requests: if an authority asks for your data, we check the legal basis of the request before any disclosure and only disclose what we are legally required to. We inform you beforehand where legally permitted (DPA clause 4.3).

export.title: Export formats and data structures
export.intro: Your data belongs to you. You export it yourself at any time, free of charge (terms, clauses 10.2 and 10.10):
items: CSV (semicolon, UTF-8): orders per order or per line item, reports and stocktaking – see exporting orders and reports.
DSFinV-K (ZIP with the CSV tables and index.xml) and TSE export (TAR according to BSI TR-03153) – with the Cloud TSE, see cash audit.
JSON via the REST API with an API token: data structures, fields and endpoints are described in the API reference (OpenAPI), access in API access.
Webhooks notify your system of events such as paid orders right away – see webhooks.
PDF for reports, shift plans, cash book and invoices.
export.outro: After your contract ends you can still export everything for 30 days. The fiscal archive (with the Cloud TSE) remains available for ten years. More under <deletion>account and deletion</deletion>.

switching.title: Switching providers
switching.intro: You can switch to another provider or to your own installation at any time – OpenEOS is open source and also runs on your own server. This is how switching works:
steps: Get in touch by e-mail at hello@openeos.de or via support in the app. We answer your questions about formats, interfaces and export.

Notice period: a day booking ends with the last booked day anyway, without notice. You can cancel your customer account for a switch at any time without notice – by e-mail or by deleting the organization in the customer portal; a subscription follows the notice period of the terms (clause 10.8). Both are shorter than the maximum of two months allowed under the Data Act.

Transition period of 30 days: we continue the service, support you and provide all exportable data. If that is not enough for technical reasons, we tell you within 14 working days and name a period of at most seven months. At your request we extend it once.

Retrieval and deletion: afterwards your data remains available for at least another 30 days. If you confirm earlier that the switch is complete, or when the period ends, we delete it (terms, clause 10.11).
switching.fees: No switching charges: we charge nothing for switching, providing the data or our support (terms, clause 10.12).
switching.selfhost: Self-hosting: the <selfhost>installation guide</selfhost> shows how to set up OpenEOS on your own server. The source code is on <github>GitHub</github>.

dataAct.contact: Questions about the Data Act? Write to <mail>hello@openeos.de</mail> (German or English).
